note.note:
Action Plan:
1. Arrange a face-to-face clinic appointment for a focused abdominal and pelvic examination (patient to call the support line to book). The clinician will examine and advise further investigations/treatment as indicated at that visit.
2. Patient to perform a pregnancy test today. If positive, patient to contact the service and attend immediately for assessment (urgent review if pregnancy test positive).
3. Advise urgent return/earlier review if symptoms worsen (increasing pain, vomiting, inability to tolerate fluids, faintness, fever) — attend emergency services if severe deterioration.
4. Document contraceptive method (Implanon, inserted ~1 year ago) and consider this in evaluation of irregular bleeding at face-to-face review.
5. Record allergy: amoxicillin — avoid prescribing amoxicillin; ensure allergy is highlighted in chart.
Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Severe lower abdominal (pelvic) pain, central/midline below the umbilicus, ongoing for a few days and progressively worsening; patient rates pain ≈ 8/10.
- Associated symptoms: Nausea (no vomiting), light vaginal bleeding/spotting (light pink), small amount of vaginal discharge, recent constipation last week now improved.
- Onset/duration/progression: Began a few days ago, constant pain, getting worse.
- Menstrual/obstetric history: Last period ~2–3 weeks ago; no prior pregnancies. Patient had a pregnancy test ~1 month ago (result not documented).
- Sexual history/contraception: Sexually active; recent intercourse reported (some confusion about timing; patient said “4 days ago” at one point). Contraception: Implanon implant in place for ~1 year.
- Past medical/surgical history: No chronic medical conditions reported; no prior surgeries.
- Allergies: Amoxicillin (reported allergy).
- Medications: Implanon (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Social history: Age 23, occupation: school teacher, lives with husband and his family. Alcohol/tobacco use unclear from transcript.

Objective:
- No vital signs recorded in the transcript.
- No physical examination documented (patient agreed to a face-to-face examination for abdominal/pelvic assessment).
- Investigations/results: Pregnancy test performed ~1 month ago (result not recorded). Doctor requested a pregnancy test to be done today.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Lower abdominal / pelvic pain:
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Ovarian/adnexal torsion. (DDx: "Ovarian/adnexal torsion" — High)
   - Differential diagnosis (from DDx, consistent with transcript):
     - Ovarian/adnexal torsion — supporting: severe, constant lower abdominal pain (8/10), progressive worsening, nausea; opposing: pain described as midline rather than clearly unilateral, no exam or imaging documented.
     - Ruptured or hemorrhagic ovarian cyst — (DDx: Medium) — supporting: acute pelvic pain and spotting possible; opposing: onset described over days rather than abrupt, no imaging.
     - Acute appendicitis (atypical) — (DDx: Low) — less likely given central pain and absence of classic migration/right-sided signs.
     - Constipation-related pain — (DDx: Low) — history of constipation last week but improving; less likely to explain current severity.
   - Investigations planned:
     - Immediate: pregnancy test today (requested by doctor).
     - Face-to-face abdominal and pelvic examination arranged; further investigations (e.g., targeted pelvic/TV ultrasound, bloods) to be performed as clinically indicated at the in-person assessment.
   - Treatment planned:
     - No pharmacologic treatment documented in the transcript. Management to be determined after in-person assessment.
   - Referrals:
     - Arrange urgent clinic review / face-to-face assessment. Escalate to emergency services if clinical deterioration.

2. Vaginal bleeding / spotting:
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Ectopic pregnancy (tubal). (DDx: "Ectopic pregnancy (tubal)" — Medium)
   - Differential diagnosis (from DDx, consistent with transcript):
     - Ectopic pregnancy — supporting: vaginal spotting and pelvic pain in reproductive-age sexually active woman; opposing: no haemodynamic instability reported, pregnancy test not up-to-date.
     - Contraceptive implant side effects (Implanon irregular bleeding) — (DDx: I2, item: "Contraceptive implant side effects") — supporting: Implanon commonly causes irregular/light bleeding; may explain light spotting; opposing: does not typically cause severe constant pain.
     - Early pregnancy complication / spontaneous abortion — (DDx: E) — possible if pregnant.
   - Investigations planned:
     - Pregnancy test today (requested). If positive, urgent assessment and likely transvaginal ultrasound per local protocols (to be arranged at face-to-face/urgent review).
   - Treatment planned:
     - No treatment documented until pregnancy status and in-person assessment determined.
   - Referrals:
     - Urgent assessment if pregnancy test positive; pelvic examination and imaging as indicated.

3. Constipation / recent gastrointestinal symptoms:
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Constipation / gastrointestinal cause. (DDx: "Constipation / colonic pain" — Low)
   - Differential diagnosis (from DDx, consistent with transcript):
     - Constipation — supporting: patient reported constipation last week which has since improved; opposing: constipation improving yet severe constant pain persists, making GI cause less likely as sole cause.
     - Appendicitis atypical — already listed under pain (DDx: Low).
   - Investigations planned:
     - No specific investigations documented for constipation in transcript; will be reassessed at face-to-face visit.
   - Treatment planned:
     - None documented.

4. Contraceptive implant (Implanon) — irregular bleeding consideration:
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Contraceptive implant-related irregular bleeding. (DDx: "Contraceptive implant side effects" — likelihood per DDx: listed under I2)
   - Differential diagnosis:
     - Implant-related bleeding — supporting: Implanon in situ; common cause of irregular/light bleeding.
     - Other gynecologic causes (ectopic, ovarian cyst, PID) — to be excluded as above.
   - Investigations planned:
     - Review of implant history and menstrual pattern at face-to-face visit; pregnancy test to exclude pregnancy-related causes.
   - Treatment planned:
     - To be determined after in-person assessment.

5. Drug allergy:
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Amoxicillin allergy (reported).
   - Differential diagnosis:
     - Reported allergy to amoxicillin; no alternative diagnoses applicable.
   - Investigations planned:
     - None.
   - Treatment planned:
     - Avoid amoxicillin and document allergy in chart.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - No vital signs recorded (BP, HR, temperature, RR, SpO2).
  - No documented pregnancy test result for the test done ~1 month ago; current pregnancy test result not yet available.
  - No physical examination findings (abdominal, pelvic, speculum, bimanual) — patient agreed to face-to-face exam which is pending.
  - No imaging (pelvic/transvaginal ultrasound) or laboratory tests documented (e.g., β-hCG, CBC, CRP) — may be required depending on in-person assessment.
  - Limited sexual/STI history (partners, STI risk) and incomplete time sequencing of recent intercourse.
- Conflicts noted between transcript and DDx:
  - DDx ranks ovarian/adnexal torsion as High likelihood. Transcript documents the pain as central/midline rather than clearly unilateral and contains no focal adnexal tenderness or exam/imaging to support torsion — clinical conflict noted.
- Transcript quality:
  - Generally intelligible though some brief unclear/inaudible phrases; patient responses about timing of intercourse and alcohol were occasionally unclear. Overall sufficient to extract key clinical information.
